metadata.title: DSCSA Implementation: Annual Reporting by Prescription Drug Wholesale Distributors and Third-Party Logistics Providers

candidates.statement: This guidance describes FDA’s expectations for prescription drug wholesale distributors 17 (wholesale distributors) and third-party logistics providers (3PLs) for the annual reporting to 18 FDA as required under the Drug Supply Chain Security Act of 2013 (DSCSA). Under section 19 584(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 360eee-3(b)), 20 beginning November 27, 2014, 3PLs must report certain information to FDA, including State 21 licensure information for each facility and the name and address for each facility. Under section 22 503(e)(2)(A) (21 U.S.C. 353(e)(2)(A) (as amended by the DSCSA), beginning January 1, 2015, 23 wholesale distributors also must report certain information to FDA, including State licensure 24 information for each facility, contact information for each facility, and any significant 25 disciplinary actions taken by a State or the Federal Government. This guidance outlines the 26 information that should be submitted to FDA, the timing of the submissions, a preferred format 27 for the submissions, and a preferred method for reporting to FDA. 28

Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should 37 be viewed only as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are 38 cited. candidates.context: Section 204 of the DSCSA amends section 503(e) of the FD&C Act and outlines requirements 49 for reporting by wholesale distributors. Section 503(e)(2)(A) of the FD&C Act (as amended) 50 requires wholesale distributors to report certain information annually, beginning on January 1, 51 204 of the DSCSA also amends section 503(e)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act and requires FDA to 55 make certain information about wholesale distributors’ licensure available to the public on 56 FDA’s Web site. Updates to the public information are to be made on a schedule to be 57 determined by FDA. 58

candidates.statement: Section 205 of the DSCSA adds section 584 to the FD&C Act. Section 584 sets forth 60 requirements for licensure and reporting by 3PLs. Under section 584(b) of the FD&C Act (as 61 amended), 3PLs must report annually to FDA, beginning on November 27, 2014 (1 year after the 62 date of enactment of the DSCSA). Third-party logistic providers must report State licensure 63 information, the name and address for each facility, and all trade names under which each 64 facility conducts business. 65

candidates.statement: Section 503(e)(2)(A) requires that any person who owns or operates an establishment that 71 engages in wholesale distribution, as defined in section 503(e)(4) of the FD&C Act, as amended 72 by the DSCSA, must report. Companies should refer to the applicable definitions in section 73 503(e)(4) of the FD&C Act to determine if they conduct wholesale distribution and would be 74 required to report annually to FDA. 75

candidates.statement: Section 584 requires that any facility of a 3PL, as defined in section 581(22) of the FD&C Act, 79 as amended by DSCSA, must report. A 3PL is an entity that provides or coordinates 80 warehousing, or other logistics services of a product 2 in interstate commerce on behalf of a 81 manufacturer, wholesale distributor, or dispenser of a product, but does not take ownership of the 82 product, nor have responsibility to direct the sale or disposition of the product. 83
candidates.context: B. Third-Party Logistics Providers 77 2 Product as defined under section 581(13) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 360eee), as amended by the DSCSA.

candidates.statement: Any person or entity that acts as both a wholesale distributor and a 3PL is subject to the reporting 88 requirements of both section 503(e)(2) and section 584. The person or entity should report 89 according to the relevant requirement for each respective facility. If a company conducts both 90 prescription drug wholesale distribution and 3PL services from the same facility, that facility 91 should be reported separately under each category as a wholesale distributor and a 3PL. 92

candidates.statement: State license information must be provided for each State from which the drug products are 187 distributed with State licensure programs and for each State that requires a license to ship 188 product into that State. Third-party logistics providers are considered to be licensed under 189 section 582(a)(7) of the FD&C Act (as amended) (21 U.S.C. 360eee-1) until the effective date of 190 the 3PL licensing regulations and may not have information to report to FDA about specific 191 State licensure unless a State has a 3PL licensing program. However, 3PLs are still required to 192 report to the FDA under the DSCSA. 193

The current unique facility identifier preferred by FDA is 183 the D-U-N-S® number. candidates.statement: Significant disciplinary actions taken against wholesale distributors must be reported to FDA, as 207 required under section 503(e)(2)(ii) of the FD&C Act, as amended by the DSCSA. In addition, 208 FDA is requesting that 3PLs report significant disciplinary actions to FDA. It is important for 209 FDA and others to know whether a wholesale distributor or 3PL has had a license revoked or 210 suspended or whether a wholesale distributor or 3PL has had any other significant disciplinary 211 actions taken against them that limits the ability of a facility to conduct drug-related business. 212 Reports of significant disciplinary actions should include any action by State or Federal 213 government that limits or prevents a wholesale distributor or 3PL from distributing or facilitating 214

candidates.statement: FDA is providing a method to enter and submit the required and voluntary reporting and 272 significant disciplinary actions for wholesale distributors and 3PLs. A link to the Web portal can 273 be accessed from FDA’s Web site. Wholesale distributors and 3PLs should access FDA’s Web 274 page at http://www.fda.gov/wdd3plreporting and follow the instructions to complete the required 275 and voluntary reporting. Companies using the FDA Web portal for entry and submission will 276 not have to convert the information to XML in the SPL format; appropriate formatting will 277 happen automatically via the web portal. This portal will allow a company to act as a reporter 278 for all of the facilities that they own without having to create a separate account for each facility. 279 If the reporter wants to enter information for multiple facilities, contact information about the 280 reporter, including the reporter’s UFI, will be needed. An alternative method for reporting is to 281 submit an XML file in the SPL format via an account through the FDA Electronic Submissions 282 Gateway (ESG). If you want to use an alternative method for your submissions, contact FDA via 283
